title: Free food festival to fill Ashbourne Market Place on August bank holiday Monday
dek: Ashbourne Food Festival brings food, drink, artisan stalls and live entertainment to the Market Place on Monday 31 August, and entry is free.
bodyHtml:
The August bank holiday has a centrepiece in Derbyshire this year. Ashbourne Food Festival takes place in the Market Place, Ashbourne, on Monday 31 August 2026, bringing food, drink, artisan stalls and live entertainment to the heart of the market town, and entry is free.

The organisers describe it as a fun free day out for the whole family, set in what they call the beautiful market town of Ashbourne at the foot of the Peak District. The recipe is a simple one: things to eat, things to drink, artisan makers to browse and entertainment alongside. On a bank holiday Monday, with nothing to pay on the way in, that is an easy day to say yes to.

The setting does a fair bit of the work too. Holding the festival in the Market Place puts it right in the middle of town rather than in a field on the edge of one, and Ashbourne's position at the foot of the Peak District, as the organisers point out, makes it a natural stop for anyone spending the long weekend out in the hills.

Free entry matters for families in particular. There is no gate price to justify, so you can wander in, see what takes your fancy and treat the day as casually or as greedily as you like. The late August bank holiday is the last one before Christmas, the weekend most of us want to make count, and a food festival in a market square is a low-effort way to do exactly that.

What we know so far

Not a great deal more, in truth. The listing is short and to the point, and no opening times or trader line-up have been published yet. If you are building your bank holiday plans around it, keep an eye on the event page for updates as the day gets closer.

The essentials

  • What: Ashbourne Food Festival, with food, drink, artisan stalls and live entertainment
  • When: Monday 31 August 2026, the August bank holiday Monday
  • Where: Market Place, Ashbourne, Derbyshire
  • Entry: free

Full details and any updates are on the Ashbourne Food Festival event page. Bank holiday Mondays built around good food rarely disappoint, and this one will not cost you a penny to walk into.

title: Pub garden market at the Prince George in Tattenhoe this August bank holiday weekend
dek: The Prince George in Tattenhoe, Milton Keynes hosts a garden pop-up market on Saturday 29 August, with live music, face painting and seasonal food.
bodyHtml:
The Prince George in Tattenhoe is turning its pub garden into a marketplace for the August bank holiday weekend. The Pints & Pop-Up Market takes place on Saturday 29 August at the pub on Portishead Drive, with stalls set up in the garden, live music during the day, face painting and seasonal food and drink served by the pub itself.

Pub garden markets are a neat format. The venue supplies the tables, the atmosphere and the refreshments, the traders supply the browsing, and visitors get a relaxed day out that needs very little planning. On the Saturday of a bank holiday weekend, that is an appealing combination.

Stalls in the garden, food from the pub

The organisers say the market brings together all kinds of sellers in what they describe as their spacious pub garden, so expect a varied mix of traders rather than a single theme. There is one deliberate exception: the stalls will not be selling food, drink or alcohol, though the organisers note that long-life food may be an occasional exception. That side of the day stays with the Prince George, which will be serving seasonal food and drinks while you browse.

For visitors, that split works rather well. You can take your time over the stalls, then settle at a garden table with something from the pub instead of juggling shopping bags and a paper plate. It also keeps the refreshments in one place, so nobody in your party has to queue in three different spots to get fed and watered.

Music, face painting and a bank holiday feel

Live music will run in the garden during the day, and there will be face painting too, which makes this an easy outing with children in tow. The listing does not include a stall list or a running order, so part of the pleasure will be seeing what turns up on the day.

The timing is worth noting as well. The late August bank holiday is the last one of the summer, and the market falls on the Saturday, which leaves the Sunday and the bank holiday Monday free for whatever else the long weekend brings. If the weather behaves, a garden full of stalls with music drifting across it is a pleasant way to open the weekend.

Plan your visit

  • When: Saturday 29 August 2026
  • Where: Prince George, Portishead Drive, Tattenhoe, Milton Keynes MK4 3FA

Opening times and entry details have not been listed yet, so it is worth checking the event page nearer the day before you set out.

You can find the full listing for the Pints & Pop-Up Market on Spaces Please.

title: Summer market comes to the Pulham Patch near Diss on Saturday 22 August
dek: Independent makers, artists and food vendors from Norfolk and Suffolk set up at The Pulham Patch near Diss on Saturday 22 August, 10am to 4pm.
bodyHtml:
The Pulham Patch, on Wood Lane near Diss, hosts a market on Saturday 22 August, with stalls open from 10am to 4pm. Independent makers, artists, food vendors and small businesses from across Norfolk and Suffolk will set up for the day, and parking is free.

One patch, two names

First, a word on the name, because this event carries two. The listing is titled the Pulham Patch Wildflower Picking Market, while the organisers' own description introduces the day as the Pulham Patch Summer Market, with the emphasis squarely on shopping, good food and supporting local businesses. Both names point to the same Saturday at the same spot, so there is no confusion about where to be. If the flower-picking side of things is what catches your eye, it is worth checking the event page for the latest details before you set off; the market itself, at least, is spelled out clearly.

Makers from across Norfolk and Suffolk

The stall line-up draws from two counties. The organisers say the market brings together a selection of independent makers, artists, food vendors and small businesses from across Norfolk and Suffolk. Handmade gifts, homeware, artisan food, jewellery and clothing are all promised, along with one-off finds for anyone after something unique.

That makes it a sensible stop for anyone with birthdays to buy for, a kitchen shelf to fill or simply a weakness for things made by hand. The organisers' pitch is a familiar one, and none the worse for it: shop small, support local, and take home something with a real person behind it rather than a barcode.

Food gets equal billing with the browsing. The listing promises great food alongside the shopping, and visitors are encouraged to pick up something to eat from the vendors and take the day at a gentle pace. The setting does half the work here: the organisers describe beautiful surroundings and a relaxed day out in the countryside, and suggest bringing family and friends along to make a proper outing of it.

Plan your visit

  • When: Saturday 22 August 2026, 10am to 4pm
  • Where: The Pulham Patch, Wood Lane, Diss IP21 4XU
  • Parking: free parking on site

It is a one-day event, so there is no second chance on the Sunday. The listing does not mention an entry fee, so have a look at the event page before travelling if that matters to your plans. And since the organisers make much of the countryside setting, dressing for the outdoors seems a fair bet.

Full details are on the Pulham Patch market page on Spaces Please.

A closing note for traders: the market is currently open for applications, so makers, artists, food vendors and small businesses after a pitch in the patch can apply directly through the event page.

title: Brew and Friends makers market takes over The Halls Norwich this September
dek: More than 50 independent businesses fill The Halls in Norwich on Saturday 5 and Sunday 6 September, with free entry, dogs welcome and full accessibility.
bodyHtml:
There is a treat coming for fans of independent shopping in Norwich. The Brew and Friends makers market takes over The Halls on St Andrew's Plain on Saturday 5 and Sunday 6 September, bringing more than 50 independent businesses together for two days of browsing from 10am to 4pm. Entry is free, the venue is fully accessible, and well-behaved dogs are welcome.

That puts the market a little over six weeks away, which is just the right amount of notice to get it in the diary before the autumn calendar starts to fill up.

What you will find inside

The stalls will carry a carefully curated mix of handmade gifts, jewellery, homeware, artwork, fashion, candles, artisan food and sweet treats, with plenty more besides, according to the organisers. That spread should cover most of the people on your present list, from the friend who collects prints to the one with strong opinions about candles.

The pitch is straightforward. The organisers say the market is a place to meet local makers, support small businesses and pick up products you will not see on the high street. In practice, that means chatting to the person who poured the candle or strung the necklace before you buy it, which turns an ordinary purchase into a small vote for somebody's independent business.

It all happens indoors, in what the organisers describe as the stunning surroundings of The Halls, so an unreliable early-September forecast need not change your plans. And because the market runs across both Saturday and Sunday, you can pick the day that suits, or come back for a second look if the first visit leaves you undecided.

If two days and more than 50 businesses sounds like a lot to take in, that is rather the point. Markets of this size reward slow browsing, and with free entry there is no pressure to see everything in one go.

A relaxed day out in the city

Brew and Friends are billing this as a relaxed day out as much as a shopping trip. The listing encourages visitors to bring friends and family along and to treat the weekend as a chance to discover some of the very best independent businesses Norfolk has to offer. Free entry helps with that: you can wander in as part of a day in the city without spending a penny until something on a stall catches your eye.

Two details are worth flagging for anyone planning ahead. Well-behaved dogs are welcome, so the four-legged member of the family does not have to sit this one out, and the venue is fully accessible, so nobody needs to worry about being caught out on the day.

Plan your visit

Here is everything you need at a glance.

  • Dates: Saturday 5 and Sunday 6 September 2026
  • Times: 10am to 4pm
  • Venue: The Halls, St Andrew's Plain, Norwich NR3 1AU
  • Entry: free
  • Good to know: well-behaved dogs welcome; fully accessible venue

The market is also taking stall applications, so if you make, bake or design and fancy trading at The Halls, you can apply directly through the event page on Spaces Please.

For the full listing, and to start planning your September weekend, visit the Brew and Friends makers market page on Spaces Please.

title: Markets worth a trip: Rochester and Princes Risborough this Sunday, then East Anglia
dek: Craft and flea in Rochester and an alternative market in Princes Risborough this Sunday, plus fairs in Norwich this September and Lowestoft in October.
bodyHtml:
Two markets share this Sunday, 26 July, and they could hardly be more different. In Kent, the monthly craft and flea market returns to Peters Village Community Centre at Wouldham, Rochester, while over in Buckinghamshire, Haunted Blessings Events brings The Gathering, an alternative market of punk, goth and curiosities, to the Wades Centre in Princes Risborough. And if this weekend is already spoken for, two East Anglian dates deserve a place on the wall planner: the Brew and Friends makers market at The Halls in Norwich on 5 and 6 September, and Shooting Star Events' Autumn Craft Fair in Lowestoft on 17 October.

Here is what the organisers have shared about each one.

July Craft & Flea Market, Rochester - this Sunday

The simplest listing of the four, and sometimes that is exactly what a Sunday needs. The July edition of this monthly craft and flea market takes place on Sunday 26 July at Peters Village Community Centre, Wouldham, Rochester ME1 3AP. The organisers describe it plainly as a monthly craft and flea market in the local community centre, which tells you the essentials: craft stalls alongside flea market finds.

The listing does not give opening hours or an entry price, so it is worth checking before you set out. And because it runs every month, this is a habit worth forming rather than a one-off outing, though this Sunday is the next chance. Full details are on the July Craft & Flea Market event page, and stallholders who fancy a table can apply for a pitch there too.

The Gathering, Princes Risborough - this Sunday

Also on Sunday 26 July, Haunted Blessings Events hosts The Gathering at the Wades Centre, Wades Park, Stratton Road, Princes Risborough HP27 9AX. This is an alternative market, and the organisers have been deliberate about who they wanted behind the stalls. Their call-out asked for traders specialising in alternative fashion, from goth and emo through grunge, steampunk and cyber; punk paraphernalia, including clothing, accessories, patches and zines; music memorabilia such as vinyl, band merch, cassettes and posters; and curiosities, a category that stretches to oddities, taxidermy, dark art and bone jewellery.

In the organisers' own words, the aim is to make the market "a haven for the alternative community". If your wardrobe leans black or your shelves have room for one more peculiar treasure, this is your Sunday sorted. The listing does not mention opening times or entry prices, so check The Gathering's event page or the organisers before travelling.

Autumn Craft Fair, Lowestoft - Saturday 17 October

Looking further ahead, Shooting Star Events brings its Autumn Craft Fair to Oulton Community Centre on Meadow Road, Lowestoft, on Saturday 17 October, running from 11am to 3pm with free entry. The organisers promise handmade crafts, gifts and decorations from local makers, along with seasonal treats, and say to expect a warm community atmosphere and "plenty of lovely products to explore".

It sounds like a sensible date for picking up autumn decorations and getting an early start on gifts while supporting small businesses on the doorstep. Details are on the Autumn Craft Fair event page, where stallholders can also apply for a space.

Brew and Friends makers market, Norwich - 5 and 6 September

The biggest stated line-up of the four belongs to the Brew and Friends makers market, which takes over The Halls on St Andrew's Plain in Norwich for the weekend of Saturday 5 and Sunday 6 September. The organisers say more than 50 independent businesses will be showing a curated selection of handmade gifts, jewellery, homeware, artwork, fashion, candles, artisan food and sweet treats, with the promise of products you will not see on the high street.

The city setting makes this an easy one to build a day out around, and the practicalities are already confirmed:

  • Saturday 5 and Sunday 6 September, 10am to 4pm
  • The Halls, St Andrew's Plain, Norwich NR3 1AU
  • Free entry, well-behaved dogs welcome, fully accessible venue

Everything else is on the Brew and Friends makers market event page, and makers who want a weekend in the city can apply for a stall through the same page.

Two reasons to leave the house this Sunday, then, and two dates to hold for later in the year. Listings do change, so give the event pages a final check before you travel.

title: How to book your first market stall, with three fairs taking applications now
dek: A step-by-step guide to booking your first market stall, with fairs in Norwich, Saxilby and Lowestoft taking stallholder applications now.
bodyHtml:
Booking your first market stall is one of those jobs that feels bigger than it is. The process is broadly the same across the UK: find an event that fits what you sell, read the listing carefully, get your paperwork in order and put in an application. To keep things practical, this guide uses three events listed on Spaces Please that are taking stallholder applications right now - a makers market in Norwich this September, a family fun day in Saxilby in August and a craft fair in Lowestoft in October.

Step one: pick the right event for your product

The single biggest factor in a good first day of trading is fit. A curated makers market draws people who have come out specifically to buy handmade work. A community fun day draws families filling an afternoon, where stalls share attention with music and activities. A seasonal craft fair sits somewhere in between. None of these is better than the others, but each suits different products.

Compare two live examples. The Brew and Friends makers market at The Halls in Norwich, on Saturday 5 and Sunday 6 September, is an indoor market where the organisers describe a carefully curated selection of more than 50 independent businesses selling handmade gifts, jewellery, homeware, artwork, candles and artisan food. If you make what you sell, that is your crowd. The Saxilby Family Fun Day on Saturday 22 August is a different sort of booking: an annual community event on Saxilby Public Recreation Ground in Lincolnshire, with live music, workshops, food and drink alongside a wide variety of trade stalls. The organisers there are inviting traders, makers, crafters, independent businesses, food vendors, charities and community groups, so the door is open far wider.

Step two: read the listing like a trader, not a visitor

Event listings are written for visitors, but they tell a would-be stallholder a great deal. Start with the basics: the date, the venue and the trading hours. Our three examples keep quite different hours. Brew and Friends runs 10am to 4pm on both of its days, Saxilby runs 12pm to 5pm, and the Autumn Craft Fair at Oulton Community Centre in Lowestoft, run by Shooting Star Events on Saturday 17 October, runs 11am to 3pm. Those hours shape how much stock you need, whether you can manage the stall on your own and what a fair pitch fee looks like for you.

Next, look at what visitors pay to get in. Brew and Friends and the Autumn Craft Fair both offer free entry, which tends to encourage casual browsing as well as planned trips. Listings can also give you a sense of scale, as organisers often put visitor numbers in their own copy. Saxilby's organisers, for example, say the fun day attracts around 2,500 visitors each year. Finally, the event page sets out the spaces on offer, so you can see exactly what you would be applying for before you commit.

Step three: know what organisers are looking for

Organisers are curating a day out, not just filling a field, and the best listings tell you what they want. Saxilby's is refreshingly direct: the organisers say they are looking for quality traders, makers, crafters, independent businesses, food vendors, charities and community groups to help create a great experience for visitors, and that interactive demonstrations and hands-on workshops are welcome. When you apply anywhere, describe clearly what you sell, show your work at its best and explain why it suits that particular event. Many organisers also balance their line-up so no single category dominates, which is a good reason to apply early rather than the week before.

Step four: sort public liability insurance

Public liability insurance covers you if a member of the public is injured or their property is damaged in connection with your stall. Organisers commonly require stallholders to hold it, and many will ask to see your certificate before confirming a pitch or letting you set up. If you do not have cover yet, arrange it before you start applying and keep a copy of the certificate with your stall kit. Requirements vary between events, so check what each organiser asks for rather than assuming one policy fits all.

Step five: apply through the event page

When an event on Spaces Please is open for applications, you apply directly through its event page. You set out who you are and what you sell, the organiser reviews your application and confirms whether you have a space. The first application is the hardest one to send; after that you have a profile and a routine, and every one after it gets quicker.

All three of the events in this guide are taking stallholder applications now:

  • Brew and Friends makers market at The Halls, St Andrew's Plain, Norwich - Saturday 5 and Sunday 6 September, 10am to 4pm - apply on the event page
  • Saxilby Family Fun Day, Saxilby Public Recreation Ground, Lincolnshire - Saturday 22 August, 12pm to 5pm - apply on the event page
  • Autumn Craft Fair, Oulton Community Centre, Lowestoft - Saturday 17 October, 11am to 3pm - apply on the event page

Pick the one that fits what you make or sell, read the listing twice and send that first application. Your first stall is closer than you think.

title: Saxilby Family Fun Day returns on 22 August with live music, stalls and workshops
dek: The annual Saxilby Family Fun Day brings live music, workshops, food and trade stalls to Saxilby Public Recreation Ground on Saturday 22 August, 12pm to 5pm.
bodyHtml:
Saxilby Family Fun Day returns on Saturday 22 August, bringing live music, workshops, food and drink and a wide variety of trade stalls to Saxilby Public Recreation Ground on William Street. The annual community event, held in the village near Lincoln, runs from 12pm to 5pm and attracts around 2,500 visitors each year.

That visitor figure is worth pausing on. For a village fun day, 2,500 people is a serious turnout, and it goes a long way to explaining why the event has become such a fixture in Saxilby's calendar. The organisers describe it as a popular annual event in the heart of the village, and this year's edition lands squarely in the school summer holidays, just when families are running out of ideas for keeping everyone entertained.

What to expect on the day

The afternoon covers the classic fun day ground, and covers it generously. There will be live music, family-friendly activities and workshops, and food and drink to keep everyone fuelled in between. Alongside the entertainment, visitors can browse a wide variety of trade stalls and meet local community organisations, which makes the event as good a place as any to find out what is going on in and around Saxilby.

The organisers say interactive demonstrations and hands-on workshops are also welcome from stallholders, so the day should offer plenty to join in with rather than simply watch. Between the music, the activities and the food, it is the kind of event where a quick look around quietly turns into the full afternoon.

It is an easy day out to recommend to different kinds of visitor, too. Families get activities and workshops aimed squarely at them, anyone who likes a browse gets a broad run of trade stalls to work through, and the presence of community groups gives the day a purpose beyond shopping and snacking. The organisers say they want the event to be a great experience for visitors, and the crowds it draws year after year suggest it delivers.

Everything happens on the Public Recreation Ground on William Street, and with five hours to play with from midday, there is no need to arrive on the dot of opening to get the best of it. As with any event held out on the rec in an English August, a glance at the forecast before you set off will not go amiss.

Stallholders, makers and community groups wanted

If you are usually on the other side of the trestle table, this one deserves a look. The organisers are actively recruiting traders, makers, crafters, independent businesses, food vendors, charities and community groups for this year's event, and say they are looking for quality stallholders to help create a great experience for visitors. Interactive demonstrations and hands-on workshops are also welcome.

Their pitch to sellers is a straightforward one: a friendly, well-attended community event where you can showcase your products and talk to local people face to face. Around 2,500 visitors across a five-hour afternoon is the sort of footfall many small businesses would travel a long way for, and for Lincolnshire traders it is right on the doorstep.

Plan your visit

The essentials for the day:

  • What: Saxilby Family Fun Day, an annual community event with live music, workshops, food and drink and trade stalls
  • When: Saturday 22 August 2026, 12pm to 5pm
  • Where: Saxilby Public Recreation Ground, William Street, Saxilby, near Lincoln

Full details are on the Saxilby Family Fun Day event page at Spaces Please, where traders, food vendors, charities and community groups can also apply for a space.

title: Walthamstow and Hampshire Christmas fairs and a Lowestoft wellness day seek stallholders
dek: Christmas fairs in Walthamstow and Hampshire and a wellness day in Lowestoft fall on 28 November and 5 December - and all three are open to stallholders.
bodyHtml:
Christmas might be the last thing on your mind in late July, but the winter events calendar is already taking shape. Three winter events have confirmed their dates for the end of the year: the annual Christmas Fair at Walthamstow Village Club in London on Saturday 5 December, the Ewhurst Park Christmas Fair on a 925-acre Hampshire estate on Saturday 28 November, and the Winter Wellness Event in Lowestoft, also on Saturday 28 November. All three are open for stallholder applications right now, which makes this a useful moment on both sides of the trestle table: visitors can get festive plans in the diary early, and traders can decide where to book a winter pitch.

Two of the three fall on the same Saturday, one in Hampshire and one in Suffolk, so for most people geography will settle the choice. Here is what each event is promising, and who each pitch might suit.

Christmas Fair at Walthamstow Village Club - Saturday 5 December

The most family-focused of the three is the annual Christmas Fair at Walthamstow Village Club, 76 Church Lane, E17, on Saturday 5 December. It runs from 12pm onwards and entry is free. The organisers promise a festive day out with inflatables, local business stalls, a special guest entertainer, festive treats and a bar and garden area, with plenty to see and do both indoors and outdoors. There is also the small matter of meeting Santa, which for many households will settle the argument on its own.

Full details are on the Christmas Fair event page, and the fair is currently taking stallholder applications through the same listing - a free-entry Saturday in December is not a bad day to be standing behind a stall.

Ewhurst Park Christmas Fair, Tadley - Saturday 28 November

A week earlier in Hampshire, Ewhurst Park near Tadley holds its Christmas Fair on Saturday 28 November. The setting is the headline here: a 925-acre rural estate run as a nature restoration project with biodiversity at its heart. The fair gathers local makers, producers and independent businesses alongside food, drink and festive activities for all ages, and the organisers describe a joyful day of organic food and festive crafts, rooted in nature and community.

Entry is £5 on the door, and children can visit Santa for £15 per child. The full listing is on the Ewhurst Park Christmas Fair page, and traders can apply for a stall there now - one for food producers and craft makers in particular, given the fair's emphasis on organic food and festive crafts.

Winter Wellness Event, Lowestoft - Saturday 28 November

On the same Saturday over in Suffolk, Oulton Community Centre on Meadow Road in Lowestoft takes a quieter approach to the run-up to Christmas. The Winter Wellness Event is billed as a day for visitors to nourish mind, body and soul, with health and wellbeing stalls, holistic therapies, mindfulness and relaxation, plus gifts and crafts for anyone making an early start on presents. The organisers call it a space of peace and harmony before Christmas, and the practicalities are gentle too: free parking, a fully accessible venue and refreshments available on the day.

The Winter Wellness Event page has the listing, and applications are open for stallholders - an obvious fit for holistic therapists, wellbeing businesses and makers of calming, giftable things.

Why book a pitch in July

Applying for a winter event while the sun is still out can feel premature, but festive dates are typically the first a maker settles in the calendar, and these organisers are clearly building their line-ups now. All three events are taking applications through their Spaces Please event pages, and they suit noticeably different traders, so the choice is less about which is best and more about which crowd you want in front of your table.

At a glance:

  • Saturday 28 November: Ewhurst Park Christmas Fair, Tadley, Hampshire. Entry £5 on the door; Santa visits £15 per child.
  • Saturday 28 November: Winter Wellness Event, Oulton Community Centre, Lowestoft. Free parking and a fully accessible venue.
  • Saturday 5 December: Christmas Fair, Walthamstow Village Club, London E17. From 12pm; free entry.

Visitors can simply pencil in the nearest date. Traders should move sooner: the Walthamstow, Ewhurst Park and Lowestoft pages all take stallholder applications directly, and pitches for the festive season have a habit of being spoken for long before the first mince pie.

title: Elves, knights and ballroom dancing: Chippenham Fantasy Ball comes to The Neeld in 2027
dek: The Gathering of the Kingdoms brings ballroom dancing, quests and costume competitions to The Neeld in Chippenham on 27 February 2027, for ages 16 and over.
bodyHtml:
The Chippenham Fantasy Ball, billed as The Gathering of the Kingdoms, is coming to The Neeld in Chippenham on Saturday 27 February 2027. The organisers are promising an evening of ballroom dancing, themed quests and costume competitions for fantasy fans aged 16 and over, and the project will initially be funded through a Kickstarter campaign launching on Friday 28 August 2026.

The listing invites guests to step beyond the ordinary for an evening of fantasy, music and imagination, with elves, knights, wizards, fae, druids, adventurers and countless other fantasy characters expected to gather under one roof. Alongside the ballroom dancing there will be themed quests to follow, costume and creative competitions to enter, a raffle, atmospheric entertainment and fantasy photo opportunities for anyone who wants a proper record of their night in another realm.

It is created, the organisers say, for fantasy lovers, costumers, crafters and anyone who has ever dreamed of attending a real fantasy ball. That last group may be larger than Chippenham suspects. Their sign-off sets the tone nicely: which kingdom will you represent?

Costumes welcome, but never compulsory

The dress code is simply fantasy, and the organisers have gone out of their way to keep it approachable. Inspiration can run from The Lord of the Rings and Merlin through to historical, mythical, woodland and cosy fantasy styles. Elaborate costumes are welcome, but they are not required - guests are free to interpret the theme in whatever way feels comfortable and affordable. A full suit of armour and a favourite cloak from the back of the wardrobe are, in other words, equally valid ways to arrive.

The creative competitions should particularly appeal to the costumers and crafters the organisers have in mind, and the promised photo opportunities mean a hand-stitched cloak or home-forged crown will not go undocumented.

A ball without a bar

Two details make this a different sort of night out. The event will be alcohol-free and food-free, and it is open to guests aged 16 and over. The organisers describe it as a welcoming evening, and the emphasis lands firmly on the dancing, the quests and the company rather than the catering. Anyone hoping to waltz with a wizard will be doing so on nothing stronger than imagination, which rather suits the theme.

First, a quest of the crowdfunding kind

Before the kingdoms can gather, there is a practical chapter to complete. The ball will initially be funded through a Kickstarter campaign launching on Friday 28 August 2026, a little over a month from now, which gives the project close to six months to build momentum before the big night the following February. Crowdfunded events live or die by their launch window, so that date is the one to note for anyone who wants to see this happen.

Kickstarter rewards are also promised. The organisers say the Chippenham Fantasy Ball Facebook page is the place to watch for venue announcements, ticket information, rewards and further details.

The essentials at a glance:

  • Date: Saturday 27 February 2027
  • Venue: The Neeld, Chippenham, Wiltshire
  • Age: guests must be 16 or over
  • Dress code: fantasy, with elaborate costumes welcome but not required
  • Alcohol-free and food-free
  • Kickstarter: launches Friday 28 August 2026

Traders should take note too. The ball is open for stall applications, so makers, costumers and crafters whose wares would suit a hall full of elves and adventurers can apply now through the Chippenham Fantasy Ball event page. For everyone else, there are seven months to plan an outfit, a Kickstarter to keep an eye on from 28 August, and a kingdom to choose.

title: School holiday days out: Spalding charity festival, fun days and a free Walthamstow fair
dek: Charity football and music in Spalding this Saturday, fun days in Cheadle Hulme and a free Walthamstow fair, plus a September dog day near Newmarket.
bodyHtml:
The summer break is under way, the children need entertaining, and the events diary is filling up nicely. Here are three school holiday outings landing within the next ten days, plus one village hall date for the autumn that is worth writing down now: the Forever Festival at Young Don's FC near Spalding this Saturday 25 July, the Schools Out Fun Day at Mickerbrook in Cheadle Hulme on Thursday 30 and Friday 31 July, the Start of Summer Fair at Walthamstow Village Club on Saturday 1 August, and a Fun Dog Day at Kirtling village hall near Newmarket on Saturday 26 September.

Where the listings mention entry at all, it is free, which never hurts in that long stretch between the end of term and September.

Forever Festival, Spalding: charity football and music this Saturday

The pick of the weekend is in Lincolnshire. On Saturday 25 July, Young Don's FC on Town Dam Lane in Donington, near Spalding, hosts the Forever Festival, a charity football and music festival raising money for Tom's Trust, which supports the wellbeing of children and their families after a brain tumour diagnosis.

The bill is a cheering one. Two celebrity football matches are planned across the day, with live music running throughout, so there should be no quiet spells in the programme. Topping it all are two headliners with serious nostalgia pull: So Solid Crew, the garage collective who soundtracked the early 2000s, and Kevin and Perry Official. It is not every weekend a Lincolnshire football ground lands a line-up like that, and it is all in aid of a cause that will be close to many families' hearts.

The organisers say there will be lots of stalls too, so expect plenty to browse between fixtures. Full details are on the Forever Festival event page.

Schools Out Fun Day, Cheadle Hulme: 30 and 31 July

Over in Greater Manchester, Mickerbrook in Cheadle Hulme hosts the Schools Out Fun Day across two days, Thursday 30 and Friday 31 July, dates that fall squarely in the school holidays, which is presumably the point of the name. The listing itself is a short one - the organisers simply point visitors to their event poster - so beyond the dates and the venue there is little we can pass on. If you are nearby and need to fill a couple of days in the holidays, keep an eye on the Schools Out Fun Day event page for anything more.

Start of Summer Fair, Walthamstow: free entry on 1 August

The following Saturday, 1 August, Walthamstow Village Club on Church Lane holds its Start of Summer Fair, running from 12pm onwards with free entry for visitors.

The organisers describe a fun-filled community event with activities indoors and out: stalls from local businesses, inflatables, ice cream, a special guest entertainer for the kids, and a bar and garden area for the grown-ups. It reads like a classic club fair, the kind where the children bounce themselves tired while the adults catch up over a drink in the garden.

Entry costs nothing, and the organisers pitch the day as a chance to support local businesses and be part of a friendly community event. Full details are on the Start of Summer Fair event page.

One for the diary: Fun Dog Day near Newmarket

Further ahead, a date for the dog owners. Fun Dog Day takes place at Kirtling village hall, near Newmarket, on Saturday 26 September. The listing gives nothing away beyond the name, the date and the venue, so bookmark the Fun Dog Day event page and check back nearer the time.

Dates at a glance

  • Forever Festival, Young Don's FC, Donington, near Spalding, Saturday 25 July
  • Schools Out Fun Day, Mickerbrook, Cheadle Hulme, Thursday 30 and Friday 31 July
  • Start of Summer Fair, Walthamstow Village Club, Saturday 1 August, from 12pm, free entry
  • Fun Dog Day, Kirtling village hall, near Newmarket, Saturday 26 September

All four listings live on Spaces Please, and each event page will carry whatever the organisers share next. That makes three chances to wear the children out before August properly gets going, and one tail-wagging Saturday to look forward to once school is back. If the weather holds this weekend, Donington looks the place to be.
